# Current state

As of 2026-10-08, research covers computer-use products and models, GUI grounding, web/mobile/desktop benchmarks, methods, safety, automation, file search, terminal UI painting, Bend, Cursor's pstack plugin, and AI-for-math manuscript releases. The computer-use archive includes `products.md`, `benchmarks.md`, `methods.md`, six `part_*.md` reports, consolidated `tldr.md` and `notes.md`, and a 331-line `sources.md` index. Research commits include `c7996f6`, `698b631`, `5a6526d`, `fbab04e`, `01eaefa`, `0b26fd3`, `502bce0`, `d25126e`, `2a5b311`, `99a632f`, `4bba324`, `30b269b`, `774e9da`, `d7d96a8`, and `962c9bc`.

The repository has a separate learning area under `learning/`. The math path under `learning/math/` contains a README, plan, progress log, problem-set and answer conventions, and a notes directory intended as a possible future iPad-sync target. This was committed as `6d446b3`. No note synchronization implementation exists.

The fff investigation found no standalone CLI, and Zeta's evaluation found no repeatable agent-level benefit, so fff was not integrated. OpenAI Decisions API evidence records public beta status. The web-agent fast-path archive records DOM-first deterministic shortlists, trigger-based image use, pre-dispatch rechecks, proposer/confirmer escalation, and defenses for marks and vision, with measurement caveats. Playwright's official actionability table confirms that `fill`, `press`, `pressSequentially`, and `setInputFiles` do not check whether the element receives events.

The TUI research found existing transcript virtualization, per-message rendering, caches, coalesced streaming paints, and final paints. The principal suspected lag sources remain full Rich re-rendering of long streaming messages, expanded agent cards rereading child transcripts on the UI loop, an O(N) transcript-prefix pass on every paint, unthrottled non-text invalidations, search restarts during revisions, repeated todo-store disk reads, unbounded render caches and output buffers, and full-frame prompt_toolkit rendering without damage tracking. These are code-reading findings, not measured fixes.

Bend language research is complete at the evidence-gathering stage. Bend v2.0.36 was installed from the Darwin arm64 release archive with SHA-256 `2876687ceb0aba836abc98b3f62c8fc9fb612d124ae2af6814d5ec937760878d`; its example run reported `ALL PROOFS CHECK`. The laws-versus-tests pilot completed one run per arm and task: arms A and B were correct for both tasks, while arm C was `feature_missing` for `pager-wrap` and correct for `ledger-fee`; the pilot was stopped and replaced by the cheaper mutation-detection experiment.

As of 2026-10-08, the Bend mutation-detection experiment is complete and committed as `d7d96a8`. It analyzed 307 valid mutants across nine programs, with 204 law-breaking, 78 law-preserving behavior changes, and 25 equivalent mutants. The two proof checkers rejected all 204 law-breaking mutants, never disagreed, and produced no soundness candidates. Example tests caught 64 of 78 law-preserving behavior changes and missed 68 of 204 law-breaking mutants. Hypothesis with 1,000 examples caught every law-breaking mutant for at least one of five seeds, although six mutants were missed by some seeds. Old proofs failed on 73 of 103 law-keeping mutants. Results are archived under `cs/programming-languages/bend/experiments/2026-10-08-mutation-detection/`, including `report.md`, `results/summary.md`, and `results/mutants.csv`. The study used machine-translated Python mirrors, a separately authored `free-shipping` program with a rare boundary, direct example-test calls, and Hypothesis without shrinking or an example database. Its behavioral ground truth came from testing rather than proof, and the translated Python was not idiomatic.

The Cursor `pstack` inspection found approximately 900K of skill files and 67,404 words across Markdown skill files. The source review and ranking are complete. The full ranking was added as `cs/agents/skills/pstack/ranking.md`, summarized in `notes.md`, and committed as `2b71bc7`. Tier-S ideas included a seven-question measurement gate, behavior-focused fake-test detection, blinded transcript-based evaluation, frozen-harness hillclimbing, encoding repeated lessons in stronger structure, and proving a change's safety-critical fact. The review retained concerns about autonomous self-merging, leaving reversible-versus-irreversible judgment to the agent, prose-only write guards, and instruction bloat.

As of 2026-10-08, the admin-v3 computer-use architecture review is complete and archived as a research artifact at `cs/agents/web-agent-fast-path/reports/foundations-reliability.md`, with raw topic reports under `cs/agents/web-agent-fast-path/reports/foundations-reliability-raw/`; the archive was committed as `d5ce6da`. The review is explicitly based on confirmed and inferred evidence and was not run on the team's stack. It identifies evidence-based step success classification, idempotency-aware action journaling, lifecycle watchdogs and reapers, real-Vercel egress testing, explicit dialog/popup/download handling, Playwright `ariaSnapshot({mode:'ai'})` with `getByRef`, checks for actionability conditions skipped by `fill`, `press`, and `setInputFiles`, unified rollover and crash recovery, and redacted per-step logging as the principal reliability changes. It retains Vercel as the preferred host based on the documented lack of a Modal path to the team's broker. Playwright validation confirmed default dialog auto-dismissal, the existence of `page.getByRef`, and release `v1.64.0` on 2026-10-07.

The admin-v3 review remains unvalidated on the team's stack. Its accepted reliability-first plan includes evidence-based outcome classes, one action wrapper with idempotency classes and a journal, lifecycle backstops and a reaper, an egress canary matrix as a release gate, dialog/popup/download policy, `ariaSnapshot` plus `getByRef` on pinned Playwright 1.64, rollover as the single recovery path, redacted per-step observability, and a BrowserHost interface while staying on Vercel. The proposed 44-task, approximately 470-run fault evaluation remains unrun and is positioned before speed work. No measured `ariaSnapshot` timings or trace-size figures are available, Browserbase proxy bypass behavior remains unknown, and the IPv6 CIDR explanation is uncertain.

The `openai/math` manuscript archive note was saved under `cs/ai-for-math/openai-math/` and committed as `314be4d`. The note reports 719 manuscripts in 372 result families, approximately 300 of 719 with Lean proofs, three withdrawals and 14 repairs after a sign error, and a mixture of formalized and unverified results. It highlights the distinction between a Lean proof of a formal statement and validation that the formal statement matches the paper's claim. The archive includes selected preprints and the reasoning trace `reasoning_traces/irrationality-exponent-of-pi.pdf` as reading material.
